text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- SMALL FIRMS SEEN HALF OF BRAZIL COMPUTER MKT BY YEAREND

Small computer firms in Brazil, many in the grey market, are battling with large multinationals for the local microcomputer market and are expected by the end of the year to have up to 50 percent of the market.
-- USA: LONG-TERM INTEREST RATE RISE BRINGS DOWN MARKETS

Emerging stock and debt markets plummeted on Wednesday due mostly to an article in the Wall Street Journal on the possibility that Japanese investors would reduce positions in U.S. debt, which would push long-term U.S. rates higher.
-- AT WTO, BRAZIL ASKS FOR TECHNOLOGY

Brazilian officials said the country needs greater access to technology from the developed world but wants to maintain its own "slow, gradual and sure pace" in entering the world's information highway.
O GLOBO
-- WAGE-EARNERS WILL PAY MORE INCOME TAX IN 1997
Wage-earners will be paying more income tax in 1997 as the government does not intend to adjust the tax tables to account for inflation during the period.
-- BRAZIL REJECTS U.S. PRESSURE AT WTO CONFERENCE

Brazil, upset with pressure from the United States to radically reduce tariffs on 4,000 products, has decided to halt negotiations at the World Trade Organization over the further opening of the Brazilian market.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PANEL ASKS FOR OUSTER OF LAWMAKER IN CORRUPTION SCANDAL
An investigating committee of Congress' lower house will recommend the ouster of PTB party lawmaker Rep. Pedrihno Abrao, who is accused of soliciting a bribe from a construction firm.
-- BRAZIL'S CARDOSO NAMES DOCTOR AS NEW HEALTH MINISTER
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has named medical doctor Carlos Cesar Albuquerque, 56, as the country's new halth minister.
-- PORTUGUESA BEATS GREMIO 2-0 IN NATIONAL TITLE MATCH
Portuguesa defeated Gremio 2-0 at Sao Paulo's Morumbi stadium in the first match in the Brazilian national championship final.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
